rows: Think of a lab bench. Change one reagent and the whole reaction moves. What is your reagent?
Brawling is like a catalyst. A little is useful. Too much, and the whole solution goes cloudy.
A risk is like a dodgy shelf. It might hold, but I would not put my weight on it.
Slow is like a long, gentle reaction. It takes patience, and I enjoy it.
The people are the ones who eat the meal. They should get something they enjoy.
I have run the reaction, and I know what it produces.
I am not the loudest thing on the bench, but I know my method.
Test the stance, as a chemist would. It is the way I weigh the powders: carefully.
Technique, the method's base. Which reagent do you rely on when the reaction goes wrong?
Strikes are the heat. Too much and everything burns. Where do you stop?
A risk without a fallback is like a reaction without a control. Who is watching it?
A stall is a flask left on the shelf. Nobody gets fed.
The people have a right to a result they understand. Let me show you the method.
You call yourself among the best, the purest sample. Let us test it and see.
Proud of your {strength}, a good ingredient. That is a good reagent. I know exactly what to do with it.
I have tasted your {strength} twice. It is good, but it needs a pinch of something else.
Composed, like a steady flame under a flask. Well balanced. It keeps the flask from boiling over.
Noted. We agree on the first reagent, which is a start.
I could tell you what I think of the method. I would rather let you test it.
One fall, one variable. Clean method, clear result. Keep me down and I will say the result was good.
On the mat, every step is a stir. Keep up with me.
Grounded or standing, the method still starts with the first grip.
Stay in front of me and show me your next reagent.
That answer is balanced enough. It is well balanced.
The sample still has no answer. The sample is going cold.
Noted. I will take that reagent on board.
Understood. It is a fair place to start the experiment.
I will run this match slowly and finish it properly.
My approach is gentle and steady. I will show you the method.
Whatever happens, you will know what went into it.
The sample is not ready yet. One more reagent to add.
I have one more reagent in mind. You will test it when the bell rings.
